blindSummary:
This country is a very safe destination, with one of the region's strongest legal frameworks for trans people. Legal gender recognition has worked by self-determination since 2018, with no medical requirements, and notably the process is open to foreign nationals as well as citizens. Discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity is banned across employment, goods, services, education, and health; a national LGBTI action plan has operated since 2018; an equality body handles complaints.

No traveler-facing concerns exist: no bathroom laws, no border issues within the region's passport-free travel area, no documented anti-trans violence pattern. Gaps are minor: no non-binary marker, and gender expression and sex characteristics are not explicitly covered in anti-discrimination law.
blindSourceSummaries: Official government portal page on applying to change one's gender status and first name(s) in the civil register - the administrative procedure for legal gender recognition in this country.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): marriage and adoption; self-determination-based gender markers (no non-binary markers); discrimination banned on sexual orientation and gender identity but not gender expression or sex characteristics; no measures on conversion practices or intersex interventions; in July 2025 the government unveiled a comprehensive LGBTIQ+ action plan, criticised by organisations for missing depathologisation and other key elements.

A national LGBTIQ+ support centre's submission to the UN human-rights review (April 2023): describes the organisation's services and the country's equality laws (employment, goods and services, education, health), the equality body and the national LGBTI action plan.

Independent LGBTQ+ travel-safety index (updated June 2023): 400+ hours of research ranking all countries' laws for LGBTQ+ traveller safety, with a companion global transgender-rights index - a comparative data source covering this country.

National daily (June 2019): report that sanctions for anti-LGBT attacks are expected to be tightened - the country's law lacks aggravating circumstances for LGBTphobic offences; victims under-report; the justice minister signalled the law would evolve after a regional human-rights monitoring body's 2017 intervention.

National daily (May 2017): the justice minister presented a bill allowing trans and intersex people to change civil-status gender by declaration - replacing the long, costly judicial procedure; welcomed by community organisations.

National daily (July 2018): the legislature approved the gender-recognition bill simplifying gender and first-name changes for trans people (57-3, only a single small party opposed) - change by written request with supporting documents, no medical requirements.
blindLocalsOnly: The self-determination legal-gender-recognition process (notably open to foreign nationals) is resident-facing administrative law.
